title: Multi-omics Data Analysis
summary_html:
The omics revolution produces data faster than it produces understanding. Turning a mass spectrometer's output into a biological claim takes a chain of decisions — how to process, filter, normalise, test, annotate and integrate — and each link in that chain can change the answer.

This three-day intensive course offers practical, up-to-date training in data science applied to omics data, with a focus on mass-spectrometry proteomics and metabolomics and on multi-omics integration.

title: Graph Machine Learning (DTU 27666 AI-guided Protein Science)
description: This is part of an AI course
summary_html: The graph machine learning module of the DTU course 27666 AI-guided Protein Science. It introduces graph biology and how to turn biological data into graphs, graph machine learning tasks and shallow embeddings (Node2Vec, DeepWalk) with PyTorch Geometric, and graph neural networks for node- and graph-level prediction. Every session comes with a hands-on Google Colab notebook.
summary: The graph machine learning module of the DTU course 27666 *AI-guided Protein Science*. It introduces graph biology and how to turn biological data into graphs, graph machine learning tasks and shallow embeddings (Node2Vec, DeepWalk) with PyTorch Geometric, and graph neural networks for node- and graph-level prediction. Every session comes with a hands-on Google Colab notebook.
highlights: Learn node embeddings with Node2Vec and DeepWalk in PyTorch Geometric
Build graph neural networks for node and graph prediction tasks

title: Protein Language Models
summary_html: An up-to-date course at the intersection of language models and the complex world of proteins. It provides an overview of the current state of the art of protein language models, which are changing research, discovery and innovation in molecular biology.
summary: An up-to-date course at the intersection of language models and the complex world of proteins. It provides an overview of the current state of the art of protein language models, which are changing research, discovery and innovation in molecular biology.
highlights: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the synergy between language models and protein data
Equip students with the skills to leverage pre-trained models and fine-tuning for bioinformatics applications
Explore cutting-edge use cases and discover how protein language models are shaping the future of molecular biology
Understand the current limitations of the field and be prepared to tackle bioinformatics challenges

title: Networks to Study Microbes
summary_html: The goal of the course is to provide an introduction to the use of networks in microbiology. The students will receive an overview of the field of computational microbiology with special emphasis on data standardization* and data sources, and how to use graph structures to solve biological questions. Further, the students will get a hands on introduction to Python programming language and its scientific libraries. At the end of the course the students will be able to: - Use multiple data sources for studying microbes in different biological contexts - Build networks, visualize and analyse them using different tools - Use Python to extract, transform and analyse different data structures
